contract.question: Will the Liberal Party win the most seats in the next Canadian election?

selectionMethod: Significance-first editorial freeze from the original research arc; five distinct kinds of pre-result developments were chosen before running event-window calculations. No timestamp was selected or moved to obtain a larger measured response.
priorExposureDisclosure: The original research exposed broad daily-median suitability statistics and the retained raw history before this freeze. No Canada five-event window scores were run before this freeze. This is prospective relative to the fresh Canada event-window calculation, not blinded preregistration.

selectedEvents.title: Mark Carney launches his Liberal leadership campaign
selectedEvents.anchorBasis: CityNews video page reports the Edmonton launch at 6:10 p.m. MST; the UTC value is the conservative public-time anchor, corroborated by same-day AP reporting.
selectedEvents.selectionReason: A new, nationally recognizable leadership contender enters the race after the market opens, changing who could carry the governing party into the election.

selectedEvents.title: Canada announces a response to the U.S. tariff order
selectedEvents.anchorBasis: The Prime Minister's archived official page is dated February 1 and records the evening response; the end of February 1 in America/Toronto (05:00Z) is the conservative cutoff and avoids inventing a broadcast minute.
selectedEvents.selectionReason: The U.S. trade shock and Canada's announced retaliation turn the election story into a live sovereignty and economic test rather than a routine leadership contest.

selectedEvents.title: Mark Carney wins the Liberal leadership
selectedEvents.anchorBasis: The CPAC and Reuters event records are dated March 9; the end of March 9 in America/Toronto (04:00Z after the daylight-time change) is a conservative cutoff for the announced first-ballot result.
selectedEvents.selectionReason: The party chooses the person who will lead the Liberals into the general election, a distinct internal-vote development with clear public meaning.

selectedEvents.title: The Governor General dissolves Parliament and calls the election
selectedEvents.anchorBasis: The Governor General's official record is dated March 23; same-day Associated Press reporting corroborates the snap election call. The end of March 23 in America/Toronto (04:00Z) avoids a made-up signing time. The former Axios retrieval was a Cloudflare challenge and is excluded.
selectedEvents.selectionReason: The constitutional trigger converts the comeback narrative into a defined campaign with an April 28 endpoint.

selectedEvents.title: Carney announces Canada's response to U.S. auto tariffs
selectedEvents.anchorBasis: The Prime Minister's official release is dated April 3; AP's contemporary report supplies the retained 16:24:16 UTC publication cutoff.
selectedEvents.selectionReason: A concrete campaign-period economic response tests whether the new Liberal government can protect workers while managing the trade war.

evaluatedButExcluded.title: Mark Carney is sworn in as prime minister
evaluatedButExcluded.reason: The official March 14 ceremony is a real and usable fact, but it formalizes the March 9 leadership result and its full measurement span overlaps that card. It is retained in the evidence manifest and candidate narrative as an evaluated alternative, not silently treated as a selected answer.
